sanskrit: ya indra iva deveṣv eti goṣu vivāvadat | tasya ṛṣabhasyāṅgāni brahmā saṃ stautu bhadrayā ||
english: He who moves among the gods like Indra, lowing loudly among the kine — let Brahmā praise with a blessing the limbs of that bull.

sanskrit: pārśve āstām anumatyā bhagasyāstām anūvṛjau | aṣṭhīvantāv abravīn mitro mamaitau kevalāv iti ||
english: His flanks belonged to Anumati; his haunches belonged to Bhaga; his knee-joints — Mitra declared: "These two are mine alone."

sanskrit: bhasad āsīd ādityānāṃ śroṇī āstāṃ bṛhaspateḥ | pucchaṃ vātasya devasya tena dhūnoty oṣadhīḥ ||
english: His rump belonged to the Ādityas; his haunches belonged to Bṛhaspati; his tail belonged to the god Vāta — with it he fans the herbs.

sanskrit: kroḍa āsīj jāmiśaṃsasya somasya kalaśo dhṛtaḥ | utthātur abruvan pado yad ṛṣabhaṃ vyakalpayan ||
english: His chest was Jāmiśaṃsa's; the vessel of Soma was set there; when they assigned portions to the bull, they declared his hooves to be the Utthātu.

sanskrit: gudā āsan sinīvālyāḥ sūryāyās tvacam abruvan | devāḥ saṃgatya yat sarva ṛṣabhaṃ vyakalpayan ||
english: His entrails belonged to Sinīvālī; his hide they declared to be Sūryā's — when all the gods assembled and apportioned the bull.

sanskrit: te kuṣṭhikāḥ saramāyai kūrmebhyo adadhuḥ śaphān | ūbadhyam asya kīṭebhyaś śvavartebhyo adhārayan ||
english: The gods gave his hoofs to Saramā and to the tortoises; his belly contents they sustained for the insects and for the dung-beetles.

sanskrit: śṛṅgābhyāṃ rakṣa ṛṣaty arātiṃ hanti cakṣuṣā | śṛṇoti bhadraṃ karṇābhyāṃ gavāṃ yaḥ patir aghnyaḥ ||
english: With his two horns he drives away the demons; with his eye he smites the enemy; with his two ears he hears what is auspicious — he who is the inviolable lord of kine.

sanskrit: śatayājaṃ sa yajate nainaṃ dunvanty agnayaḥ | jinvanti sarve taṃ devā yo brāhmaṇa ṛṣabham ā juhoti ||
english: He performs a hundredfold sacrifice; the fires do not afflict him; all the gods quicken him who offers oblation to the bull, O Brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāya vṛṣabhaṃ dattvā varīyaḥ kṛṇute manaḥ | puṣṭiṃ so aghnyānāṃ sve goṣṭhe vi paśyatu ||
english: Having given a bull to a Brāhmaṇa, one makes the mind more spacious; may he behold the thriving of the inviolable ones in his own cattle-pen.

sanskrit: gāvaḥ santu prajāḥ santv atho astu tanūbalam | sarvaṃ tad anu manyantāṃ devā ṛṣabhadāyine ||
english: May there be cattle; may there be offspring; and may there be bodily strength — may all the gods consent to all of that for the giver of the bull.

sanskrit: ayaṃ pipāna indriyaṃ rayiṃ bibharti cetanīm | ayaṃ dhenuṃ sudughāṃ nityavatsāṃ vaśaṃ duhe vipaścitaṃ puro divaḥ ||
english: This one, drinking in vigor, bears a wealth endowed with consciousness; this one milks the good-milking cow ever accompanied by her calf, milks the amenable one, the wise one, in front of the sky.

sanskrit: piśaṅgarūpo nabhaso vayodhā aindraḥ śuṣmo viśvarūpo na āgan | prajām asmabhyaṃ dadhad rayiṃ ca rāyaspoṣam upasatvā sadema ||
english: Of tawny form, sustainer of vigor from the sky, the might of Indra, all-formed, has come to us; bestowing offspring upon us and wealth, may we abide, having drawn near to the increase of riches.

sanskrit: etaṃ vo yuvānaṃ pari dadhmo atra tena krīḍantīś carata vaśām̐ anu | mā no hiṃsiṣṭa januṣā subhāgā rāyaś ca poṣair abhi naḥ sacadhvam ||
english: We place this young one here among you; roaming in delight with him, follow the amenable cows; do not harm us, O well-favored ones by your nature — attend upon us with the increase of wealth.

sanskrit: upehopaparcano 'smin goṣṭha upa pṛñcatu | upa ṛṣabhasya yad reta upendra tava vīryam ||
english: Let the Upaparcana come hither; let it mix within this cattle-pen — the seed of the bull, O Indra, that is your virile power.

sanskrit: ayaṃ pratisaro maṇir vīro vīrāya badhyate | vīryāvānt sapatnahā śūravīraḥ paripāṇaḥ sumaṅgalaḥ ||
english: This amulet-stone bound as a counter-charm is tied upon the hero for a hero's sake; possessed of virile force, a slayer of rivals, a warrior-hero, a protector, most auspicious.

sanskrit: ayaṃ maṇiḥ sapatnahā suvīraḥ sahasvān vājī sahamāna ugraḥ | pratyak kṛtyā dūṣayann etu vīraḥ ||
english: This gem is a rival-slayer, a fine hero, full of might, a prize-winner, overpowering, formidable; may the warrior come forward, deflecting and corrupting sorceries.

sanskrit: anenendro maṇinā vṛtram ahann anenāsurān parābhāvayan manīṣī | anena dyāvāpṛthivī ubhe ajayad anenājayat pradiśaś catasraḥ ||
english: With this gem Indra, the wise one, slew Vṛtra; with this he caused the Asuras to be overthrown; with this he conquered both heaven and earth; with this he conquered the four directions.

sanskrit: ayaṃ srāktyo maṇiḥ pratīvartaḥ pratisaraḥ | ojasvān vimṛdho maṇiḥ so asmān pātu viśvataḥ ||
english: This Srāktya gem, a repeller, a counter-charm — the gem full of vital force that crushes enemies: may it guard us from all sides.

sanskrit: tad agnir āha tad u soma āha bṛhaspatiḥ savitā tad indraḥ | te te devāḥ purohitāḥ pratīcīḥ kṛtyāḥ pratisarair ajantu ||
english: That Agni has declared, that Soma has declared, Bṛhaspati, Savitā, and Indra have declared it — may those gods, as your priests, drive back with counter-charms the sorceries directed against you.

sanskrit: antar dadhe dyāvāpṛthivī utāhar uta sūryam | utemaṃ brahmaṇaspatiṃ te te devāḥ purohitāḥ pratīcīḥ kṛtyāḥ pratisarair ajantu ||
english: Within himself he concealed heaven and earth, and the day, and the sun, and also this Brahmaṇaspati — may those gods, as your priests, drive back with counter-charms the sorceries directed against you.

sanskrit: ye srāktyaṃ maṇiṃ janā varmāṇi kṛṇvate | sūryo divam ivāruhya vi kṛtyā bādhate vaśī ||
english: Those persons who fashion armor with the Srāktya gem — like the sun mounting the sky, the sovereign drives away sorceries.

sanskrit: srāktyena maṇina ṛṣiṇeva manīṣiṇā | ajaiṣaṃ sarvāḥ pṛtanā vi mṛdho hanmi rakṣasaḥ ||
english: With the Srāktya gem, as with a sage endowed with wisdom, I have conquered all armies; I smite the enemies, I slay the Rakṣases.

sanskrit: yāḥ kṛtyā āṅgirasīr yāḥ kṛtyā āsurīr uta | kṛtyā yāḥ svayaṃkṛtā yā u cānyebhir ābhṛtāḥ | ubhayīs tāḥ parā yantu parāvataṃ navatiṃ nāvyā ati ||
english: Whatever sorceries are those of the Āṅgirasas, whatever sorceries are those of the Asuras, the sorceries that are self-made and those that are brought by others — may all of them pass away to the far distance, beyond the ninety navigable waters.

sanskrit: asmai maṇiṃ varma badhnantu devā indro viṣṇuḥ savitā rudro agniḥ | prajāpatiḥ parameṣṭhī virāḍ vaiśvānara ṛṣayaś ca sarve ||
english: May the gods bind the gem as armor upon him — Indra, Viṣṇu, Savitā, Rudra, Agni, Prajāpati, Parameṣṭhin, Virāj, Vaiśvānara, and all the seers.
